w: Sawai Pratap Singh built this five-story facade in 1799 after admiring the Khetri Mahal, and gave it 953 honeycombed jharokha windows so the palace women could watch festivals in the street below without ever being seen. Most visitors mistake the whole thing for a palace front -- it's really just a screen.
s: 953 windows built so no one could look back.
_facts: Built 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh, grandson of Jaipur founder Jai Singh II
953 small jharokha windows in a honeycomb pattern
Original purpose: let royal women watch street life unseen
Ventilation cooled the interior via the Venturi effect
Inspired by the Khetri Mahal; designed by Lal Chand Ustad

w: Jai Singh II moved his court here from Amber in 1727 and built this palace strictly to vastushastra rule, blending Mughal and Rajput style -- and the royal family never really left. It still houses the Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II Museum and around 500 personal staff, a working palace as much as an exhibit.
s: A palace museum the royal family still calls home.
_facts: Construction begun 1727 when Jai Singh II moved his court from Amber; completed 1732
Built to vastushastra rules, blending Mughal and Rajput architecture
Houses the Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II Museum
Royal family still resides there, with around 500 personal servants

w: Nahargarh started life as Sudershangarh, one corner of a three-fort defense ring with Amber and Jaigarh -- until construction kept failing, and locals blamed the restless spirit of Nahar Singh Bhomia. The builders raised him a memorial temple inside the walls to pacify him, and the fort took his name instead.
s: A fort renamed to pacify an angry ghost.
_facts: On the edge of the Aravalli Hills overlooking Jaipur
Formed a defense ring with Amber Fort and Jaigarh Fort
Originally named Sudershangarh, renamed Nahargarh ('abode of tigers')
Popular belief: Nahar Singh Bhomia's spirit obstructed construction until a memorial temple was built for him

w: Jaigarh's ramparts crown the Hill of Eagles above Amer Fort and Maota Lake, begun around the eleventh century after Raja Kakil Dev took the ground from the Mina tribes. Its prize exhibit is the Jaivana, once the largest cannon ever mounted on wheels -- and a hidden passage still links the fort down to Amer.
s: Home to the largest cannon ever built on wheels.
_facts: On Cheel ka Teela (Hill of Eagles), overlooking Amer Fort and Maota Lake
Construction begun by Raja Kakil Dev, mid-11th century, after capturing the region from Mina tribes
Also called Victory Fort
Houses the Jaivana cannon, once the world's largest cannon on wheels
Connected to Amer Fort by subterranean passages

w: Rajasthan's oldest museum sits in Ram Niwas Garden just outside the old city wall, an Indo-Saracenic showpiece once ranked among the best-stocked collections of the nineteenth century. A 2008 renovation turned the old Government Central Museum into one of India's most modern.
s: Rajasthan's oldest museum, in Indo-Saracenic stone.
_facts: Oldest museum in Rajasthan, functions as the state museum
Indo-Saracenic architecture, in Ram Niwas Garden opposite New Gate
Also called the Government Central Museum
Considered one of the best 19th-century museums for its collections
Renovated 2008, reopened as an advanced museum

w: Built in 1835 as a garden retreat for a queen's handmaiden, this place kept climbing the social ladder -- royal hunting lodge, then the Maharaja's principal residence, then, after independence, India's first palace hotel. Taj Hotels has run it since 1972, still trading as the 'Jewel of Jaipur.'
s: Built for a handmaiden, ended up the Maharaja's palace.
_facts: Built 1835, originally a garden retreat for a queen's handmaiden
Later a royal guesthouse and hunting lodge
Expanded early 20th century into principal residence of Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II
Converted after independence into India's first luxury 'palace hotel'
Managed by Taj Hotels since 1972; nicknamed 'Jewel of Jaipur'

w: The story goes that a sage named Galav meditated and did penance in this crevice in the hills, and pilgrims still climb the same crack in the rock today, past a chain of spring-fed sacred kunds where they bathe, up to a hilltop temple with the whole of Jaipur laid out below.
s: Sacred spring pools stacked up a hillside crack.
_facts: Ancient Hindu pilgrimage site about 10 km east of Jaipur
Temples built into a narrow crevice in the surrounding hills
Natural spring fills a series of sacred kunds (water tanks) for bathing
Hilltop temple with panoramic views of Jaipur
Believed site of the sage Galav's meditation and penance

w: Raja Man Singh I, one of Akbar's generals, carried this image of Durga home from a military campaign in Jessore -- now in Bangladesh -- and installed her inside Amer Fort in 1604. She's been Shila Devi ever since, one of the region's prominent Shakti shrines.
s: A war trophy from Bengal, enshrined since 1604.
_facts: Historic Hindu temple inside Amer Fort
Dedicated to Goddess Durga in her form as Shila Devi
Established 1604 by Raja Man Singh I, general of Mughal emperor Akbar
Idol brought from Jessore, present-day Bangladesh, after a military expedition

w: Amber's lake carried the older name Mahavata before everyone shortened it to Maota, after the stand of large trees still crowding its banks below the fort it once supplied.
s: A fort's lake, named for its trees.
_facts: Located in Amber, Rajasthan
Ancient name 'Mahavata', commonly known as Maota
Name derives from large trees near the lake

w: Part palace, part hotel, part literary pilgrimage site: the royal family that still lives here also runs it as a heritage hotel, and since 2006 its courtyards have hosted the Jaipur Literature Festival, now one of the city's best-known annual draws.
s: The palace that hosts the Jaipur Literature Festival.
_facts: Royal palace converted into a heritage hotel
Part still occupied by the royal family, who also run the hotel
Has hosted the Jaipur Literature Festival since 2006

w: Jai Singh II built this tiered, terraced garden in 1728 as a love token for his second queen, a Sisodia princess of Mewar's Suryavanshi line -- hence the name. Fountains and watercourses step down the hillside past painted pavilions, up to a two-story palace whose murals still tell the life of Krishna.
s: A garden built as a 1728 gift for a queen.
_facts: Garden and palace 6 km from Jaipur, on the Jaipur-Agra highway
Built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II in 1728 for his second queen
Tiered multi-level gardens with fountains, watercourses and painted pavilions
Double-storeyed palace with murals depicting the life of Krishna
Queen was from the Sisodia line of Suryavanshi Rajputs of Mewar

w: Open since 1877 next to the Albert Hall Museum, Jaipur Zoo has been quietly changing its mission -- its ghariyal breeding farm, started in 1999, is the fourth-largest in India, and since 2018 the whole place has been converting into a bird park. The big carnivores have already gone.
s: An 1877 zoo turning itself into a bird park.
_facts: Opened 1877, near Albert Hall Museum and Ram Nivas Garden
Divided into mammal and bird/reptile sections, around 50 species
Ghariyal breeding farm established 1999, fourth-largest in India
2018: announced conversion into a bird park with large aviaries; large carnivores already removed

w: Built in the nineteenth century as the private palace of the nobleman Raghubir Singhji, this heritage hotel sits just outside the old city walls near Chand Pol -- a quieter, family-run alternative to Jaipur's grander royal addresses.
s: A minor nobleman's palace, now a heritage hotel.
_facts: Heritage hotel built in the 19th century
Was the palace of nobleman Raghubir Singhji
Just outside the old city walls, north of Chand Pol

w: Raja Man Singh kept twelve queens and built twelve rooms to match, each with its own private staircase, inside this red sandstone and marble hill fort above Maota Lake. Its showpiece is the Sukh Niwas, cooled by a water cascade with no machinery at all -- and a gate-temple to the goddess Shila Devi.
s: Twelve queens, twelve rooms, one hill fort.
_facts: Hilltop fort in Amer, principal tourist attraction near Jaipur
Built of red sandstone and marble, laid out on four levels
Includes Diwan-e-Aam, Diwan-e-Khas, Sheesh Mahal (Jai Mandir), and Sukh Niwas cooled by a water cascade
Overlooks Maota Lake, the main water source for the palace
Shila Devi temple at the Ganesh Gate; Raja Man Singh had 12 queens and 12 rooms with staircases

w: Jai Singh II, the founder of Jaipur, built this temple to Radha and Krishna inside his own City Palace complex in the eighteenth century -- and had the deities carried in from Vrindavan itself, the town where Krishna's own legend is set.
s: A temple to Krishna, deities carried from Vrindavan.
_facts: Hindu temple dedicated to Radha and Krishna
Located within the City Palace complex, Jaipur
Established 18th century by Maharaja Jai Singh II
Deities brought from Vrindavan
